Commentary.Commentary: We are back for South Africa's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be Jemma Botha and Simone Lourens to open the innings for South Africa. Jennifer Jackson will start with the new ball. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, South Africa Women Under-19 are on the top after the first inning and they will want to chase as early as they can to boost their net run rate. On the other hand, Ireland Women Under 19 Women will want to give it a fight in defending it. Don’t go anywhere as the action for the second inning isn’t very far away.

Mieke van Voorst is up for a quick chat and says that they as a team take everything one at a time and they did well to switch on and switch off during the delay. Talking about the diving catch, she said that it looped up in the air towards her and the fielder next to her told her to stay calm and she just took it in the end. Concludes by saying that they have confidence that they will chase it down comfortably.

For South Africa Women Under-19, Monalisa Legodi was brilliant with the ball as she picked up four wickets. Skipper Kayla Reyneke also picked up three wickets with one maiden whereas Fay Cowling and Nthabiseng Nini also chipped in with a wicket each. Whether it be their ground fielding or catching, South Africa threw themselves around in the field and made it even harder for Ireland.

In a rain-shortened game, Ireland Under-19 Women have got bundled out at the score of just 35 runs in 9.4 overs. They weren't able to cash in on their decision to bat first after winning the toss. From start to finish, South Africa Under 19 Women were wonderful, giving not much away. With the game curtailed to 10 overs per side, the Irish batters had no other option but to get going straight away but it all went wrong for them.

OUT! TAKEN! Kayla Reyneke wraps up the innings! Going across the batter from around the wicket, on a nagging length, Ellie McGee lunges to work it away on the leg side with a closed bat face. Gets a leading edge that balloons and goes straight down the throat of short third where Mieke van Voorst does the rest. Kayla finishes with three wickets. Ireland have been bowled out for 35!

Commentary.Commentary: After a lengthy delay, we are all set to get going. South Africa are in a huddle near the ropes before striding out to the centre. Remember, the Powerplay will be of 3 overs. Freya Sargent and Rebecca Lowe are the two Irish openers. Nthabiseng Nini has the new ball in hand. Nini to Freya first up. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start, but before that, Kayla Reyneke and Niamh MacNulty will lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. It will be the Irish national anthem first, followed by that of South Africa.

PITCH REPORT - Jon Kent is near the deck. He informs that the overhead conditions have improved. Tells that the edge of the squares is still a bit damp and it is something the players will need to be wary of. Mentions that this venue has seen some of the best wickets of the competition. Feels that batters will get value for their shots and the deck could offer some turn.

The South African skipper, Kayla Reyneke says that they would have batted first as well but they are ready to go. Mentions that it is not a full 20 overs game but the team is raring to go. Concludes by saying that they are going with the same side.

Niamh MacNulty, the Irish skipper says that they will bat first. Adds that the group games were affected by rain and they are well prepared for these kind of conditions. Informs that there is a change with Lucy Neely coming in for Alice Walsh. Says that they just want to take the momentum from the group stage and just carry on that.

Ireland Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Julie McNally, Lara McBride, Jennifer Jackson, Annabel Squires, Lucy Neely (In for Alice Walsh), Ellie McGee, Kia McCartney, Rebecca Lowe, Abbi Harrison (WK), Freya Sargent, Niamh MacNulty (C).

South Africa Women Under-19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Simone Lourens, Jemma Botha, Diara Ramlakan, Kayla Reyneke (C), Karabo Meso (WK), Fay Cowling, Mieke van Voorst, Ashleigh van Wyk, Monalisa Legodi, Nthabiseng Nini, Seshnie Naidu.
TOSS - Ireland Women Under-19 have won the toss and they will BAT first.

UPDATE - Great news! We are going to have a game. The toss will take place at 8 am GMT, with the first ball scheduled to be bowled at 8.25 am GMT. It will be a 10-overs-per-side contest, so we can expect an action-packed affair!

UPDATE - 7.30 am GMT - The match officials are still not satisfied with the conditions, and there will be another inspection at 7.45 am GMT. The ground staff are working hard to dry up the soggy outfield, but the visuals aren’t promising. The South African players are out on the field going through their paces, which shows how eager they are to get on the park.
UPDATE - 7.25 am GMT - We are yet to hear from the ground regarding the outcome of the inspection. We are expecting the update shortly. Stay tuned.

In case you were wondering how the two Super Six groups have been formed and what's ahead, here's a quick rundown. Out of the 16 teams, 12 (top 3 from each group) have made it through to the Super Six stage. These 12 teams have been split into two groups. Teams from Groups A and D have been paired in Group 1, while teams from Groups B and C are in Group 2. All qualified teams carry forward the wins and net run rate they accumulated when they faced off against the teams that also advanced from their original group during the group stage. The top two from each of the two groups will make their way to the semifinals.

While we wait, you can switch tabs and follow the second game of the day happening in Bangi, where Australia, after opting to bowl first, have put West Indies in early trouble at 7/2. Earlier in the day at the same venue, New Zealand successfully defended a modest total of 97 against the USA. From being 73/5, the USA collapsed spectacularly, losing their last 5 wickets for just 6 runs to be rolled over for 79. This meant that off-spinner Ritu Singh’s five-wicket haul went in vain, as New Zealand pulled off a dramatic win.

Ireland's Ellie McGee is also in for a quick chat. She says that it was an unbelievable feeling to win against Pakistan in the last game. Mentions that it was a good win for them. Adds that it was definitely great to get a game after being on the sidelines and thought about needing to do something for the team and put in the work for it. Further mentions that the cuisine in Malaysia has been top tier and the nature as well.

Karabo Meso from South Africa is up for a quick chat. She says that this time, they are in a comfortable place as compared to the previous edition. Adds that If you aren’t loud enough as a keeper, the team won’t rely on you. Mentions that she comes alive on the field when the energy of her team goes down. Shares that she loves to play the sweep shots as those are her productive shots.

UPDATE - 6.23 am GMT - The ground staff have started peeling off the covers, but the outfield has taken a significant beating, and the visuals are far from promising. The overcast skies aren’t helping either, as some sun would have sped up the drying process. An inspection is scheduled for 7 am GMT. The ground staff have a tough task ahead of them, but we remain hopeful of witnessing some action today.

UPDATE - 6.17 am GMT - Not the news we were hoping for, but it is on expected lines given the conditions in Sarawak since morning. The flip of the coin has been DELAYED. The rain has stopped, but considering the downpour last night and this morning, extensive mop-up work will be required to make the ground playable.

Ireland, on the other hand, have shown character to progress, bouncing back from early setbacks. They surprised many with a crucial win over Pakistan and will look to build on that momentum. Their batting lineup has shown promise but will need greater contributions from their middle order. On the bowling side, Ireland’s attack has been effective in key moments, but consistency will be vital against a strong South African side. Stick around as we hope for better fortunes and improved conditions!

South Africa have been in formidable form, winning all three games in the group stage despite interruptions caused by rain. Their top order has delivered consistent starts, but their middle order remains largely untested, presenting an intriguing subplot as they prepare for the challenges in the Super Six stage. With the ball, their disciplined attack has stifled opponents, and their ability to strike at regular intervals has been a major asset.

Hello and welcome one and all from a wet Sarawak as South Africa Women Under-19 take on Ireland Women Under-19 at the Borneo Cricket Ground. Earlier in the day, the first game at this venue between England and Nigeria was abandoned without a ball bowled, and unfortunately, the outlook for this game doesn’t look promising either, with more rain expected to disrupt proceedings.
... MATCH DAY ...

The Super Six leg of the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup, 2025, continues with a high-stakes Group 2 clash as South Africa Women Under-19, Group C toppers, take on Ireland Women Under-19, who claimed the third spot in Group B. The match, slated as number 4 is set to take place at the scenic Borneo Cricket Ground in Sarawak, and both teams will be eager to make their mark in this crucial encounter. South Africa Women Under-19 come into this stage as one of the unbeaten teams in the tournament, riding on a wave of momentum. Despite all three of their group games being affected by rain, the Proteas have showcased dominance in every outing and will look to carry that energy forward. Jemma Botha and Simone Lourens have been the batting mainstays, providing solid starts for the team. However, skipper Kayla Reyneke is yet to make her mark with the bat, and this might be the perfect stage for her to step into the spotlight. The middle order, largely untested due to weather disruptions, faltered when given an opportunity, raising questions about their ability to handle pressure in critical moments. On the bowling front, Kayla Reyneke and Seshnie Naidu have been standout performers, ably supported by a disciplined bowling unit that has consistently stifled opposition lineups. Ireland Women Under-19, on the other hand, have shown resilience and grit to make it this far. After their opening game was washed out and a comprehensive defeat to the USA in their second, they bounced back in style, delivering a surprise victory over Pakistan in a rain-shortened match. This win has injected much-needed confidence into the side. Openers Alice Walsh and Freya Sargent have shown promise at the top, but their inability to convert starts into substantial scores remains a concern. The middle order has offered glimpses of potential but will need someone to take responsibility and anchor the innings. Ireland’s bowling unit has been steady, but they’ll need to step up and find regular breakthroughs to challenge South Africa’s strong batting lineup. While the Proteas are firm favourites heading into this clash, Ireland have shown they can deliver under pressure. Will South Africa continue their unbeaten run, or will Ireland pull off another upset? An exciting contest awaits at the Borneo Cricket Ground.
